title: Tired of one-shot prompt games? Here is a 5k prompts one
author: rainbooow
selftext:
Hi everyone,

I’ve been working on this project for almost a year, with another dev. It now has a Steam page, and release is planned in 2–3 months: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5387050/Tinymon\_Tactics](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5387050/Tinymon_Tactics/). Any wishlist is greatly appreciated!

It’s heavily inspired by Teamfight Tactics, but set in a Pokémon-like universe, solo-only, with roguelite elements.

We’ve been building it for almost a year, heavily with AI (5k+ prompts, Pro plan only). Not everything is AI though: we wrote the original codebase by hand, and made or edited many assets ourselves.

Why did it take "so long": AI makes code fast, but it doesn’t make a game fun. Well over half our time went into iterating on gameplay, balance and pacing, and several systems were rebuilt multiple times (synergies system, events, tinymons effects, etc). AI is not a magic solution there, if you want a good experience and not slop, this still requires a huge amount of time and iteration.

Anyway, pretty happy with how it currently looks, going to focus the next few months on further polishing the balance and game depth, before releasing it in the wild :).

comments.author: randomallocated
comments.body: Looks pretty neat, will wishlist.  I'm building a dnd styled roguelite game myself and struggle adjusting the core game mecanics, did you rely on ai to do that or have you used other ressources (books, YT channels, etc). Any tips appreciated

replies.author: rainbooow
replies.body:
You mean, balancing numbers, encounters difficulty, etc.?

No, I do not believe AI can help much there, this is the core of the game and what make the diff (imo) between AI slop and an actual game.   
But AI \*can\* help in speeding this up (a bit), for instance by quickly building the internal dev tools that can help you balancing the game. For instance in my case, the game is basically a Slay The Spire like map, with multiple nodes of increasing difficulty. For one of the initial balance round of the different encounters, I quickly created a simulator that would make each node fight against the N+1 and N-1 node (in theory, it should win against the N-1 and lose against the N+1), running 100 battles (as its not 100% deterministic), and surfacing the encounters that were far too weak/strong. This can be one-shotted by the AI, while it would have required me a full day to build it, probably.

But making sure that you unlock roguelite elements on a regular basis, that those elements are strong enough to actually make a diff for your next runs, without trivializing the experience? You cannot outsource that to the AI.

replies.author: rainbooow
replies.body:
Thanks for the feedback, and good catch. Indeed, the looks are not fully there yet (though it is still miles better than what we had 6 months ago, to the point that we are sometimes blind to the current flaws).

For the combat, this would definitely looks better with actual hit animations, I agree. This does require a huge amount of work, even with the help of AI (there are 150 mons in the game), and current focus is on nailing down the core gameplay.

replies.author: xens999
replies.body: I have a similar pokemon project I'm working on (not an autobattler tho), I had it build new move animations for all the moves (around 120 iirc) in about an hour or two, with a previewer etc. Its not too bad just takes a decent chunk of compute. Nailed about 60% of them on the first go and redid the rest in one go after I told it what I wanted changed.

replies.body:
If no AI was used, would you say the same thing? I am not pretending this is AAA quality, but for an indie game, this does not feel out of place, imo. Especially considering the fact that most of the time has been spent on iteraring on the gameplay, abilities, items, etc.

replies.author: Kalaminator
replies.body: Nowadays images are the way past because you just generate them. If had to give you an advise on this game to be playable for me, I'd say you need to work on the animations when there is the battle happening on the board, which is what threw me off the most. That would make it satisfying. As for the rest I need to try to have the feeling and give proper feedback.

replies.author: rainbooow
replies.body:
Thanks for the feedback. I agree with your and the other comment on animation, this can be improved to have hit reaction, small cast animation, etc. And skill effect are not all high quality yet.
But doing new spritesheet for all mons (150) to have a proper attack, walk, idle,... animation, even with AI, is going to be a huge amount of work, and i think there are other areas worth investing into instead (AI do not properly one shot this, at least it was not the case 2-3 months ago).

We are working on a demo. The game has been play tested a lot already by some friends, but the full vertical is not balanced enough yet to already share something. I will post an update when this is the case!
